simple.meaning: עָגוּר (ʻâgûwr) is a Hebrew word meaning “probably the swallow.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: עָגוּר (H5693) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Isaiah 38:14, with occurrences in Isaiah, Jeremiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עָגוּר (H5693) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in עָגוּר (H5693) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: עָגוּר (ʻâgûwr) / H5693 is traced through Isaiah 38:14, Jeremiah 8:7 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H5693. agur עָגוּר noun [masculine] apparently understood by Masoretes as name of a bird; very uncertain; crane according to Saad (Isaiah), but note of crane not suitable (Tristr NHB 239 f. ); — וְעָגוּר וְסוּס וְתוֺר Jer 8:7 ; עָגוּר כְּסוּס Isa 38:14 (but here gloss Klo Brd Di Dn Che Hpt ); Thes and (in Jeremiah) Hi Gf Gie strike out וְ and take ׳ע as adjective of סוס = twittering or the like; Thes assumes transpos. from גער , Ethiopic cry . I, II, III. עַד see I. עדה . עֵד see עוד . עֹד see עוֺד . עִדֹּא see עדד . below, עדד (√ of following; compare Arabic count, reckon , number, period ; Aramaic עִדָּנָא time ).
definitions.rootNote: passive part (but with active sense) of an unused root meaning to twitter ;

occurrences.englishText: I chattered like a swallow or a crane.
Yes, the stork in the sky knows her appointed times.
